articles.title: Recently patched PaperCut zero-days used in data theft attacks
articles.text:
Two security vulnerabilities in the PaperCut NG and MF print management software, patched last week after being exploited as zero-days, are now being abused in data theft attacks.
According to PaperCut Software, the software is used by 100 million users across more than 70,000 organizations, including large companies, state agencies, and educational institutions.
Tracked as CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078, the two security flaws can be chained to bypass authentication and gain remote code execution on vulnerable PaperCut NG and MF print management servers.
PaperCut Software released three sets of emergency patches to address the vulnerabilities on Thursday, Friday, and Tuesday, "to rush mitigations to customers who might not be able to remove their servers from the internet."
"The first release was an emergency mitigation. The next release added further hardening as we understood more," explained PaperCut CEO Chris Dance today. "We have additional work in hand, and there may be further Emergency Patch releases if required, and of course, a final fully QA and regression-tested official release soon."
The company has also published indicators of compromise to help defenders block ongoing attacks, but it has yet to attribute the attacks or explain what the threat actors are doing after compromising vulnerable servers.
"We recommend all customers with internet-facing Application Servers install Release 3 as soon as possible, even if they have already applied an earlier emergency release," the company said.
Actively exploited for data theft
Over the weekend, threat intelligence company Defused also confirmed that attackers have begun abusing the two flaws in the wild to steal data from victims' servers.
"We are observing CVE-2026-81578 / CVE-2026-82078 (PaperCut NG/MF) exploit activity in our honeypots since late yesterday UTC (Aug 29th)," Defused said. "An actor is abusing the auth bypass to hijack PaperCut's external user-lookup. Unlike the RCE path in public writeups, the actor goes for data theft - dumping DB tables via Derby."
Internet security watchdog Shadowserver currently tracks over 800 PaperCut MF and NG servers exposed online, although there is no information on how many are honeypots or have already been secured against these attacks.
Both state-backed hacking groups and ransomware gangs have previously targeted PaperCut security flaws in the wild over the last several years.
A critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE–2023–27350) and a high-severity information disclosure flaw (CVE–2023–27351) were chained in April 2023 attacks linked to the LockBit and Clop ransomware gangs.
Microsoft revealed two weeks later that the Muddywater and APT35 Iranian state-backed hacking groups had also joined the attacks.
As the company explained at the time, the threat groups abused the 'Print Archiving' feature designed to save all documents sent through PaperCut printing servers.
One month later, in May 2023, the FBI and CISA warned that the Bl00dy Ransomware gang had also begun exploiting the CVE–2023–27350 flaw for initial access to targets' networks.
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) flagged another remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2023-2533) as actively exploited in July 2025.
Update September 01, 07:27 EDT: Added info on Emergency Patch Release 3.

articles.title: Egypt’s Buzzy Party is a multi-player social gaming app focused on Arabic-speakers - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian-founded Buzzy Party is a multi-player social gaming app focused on Arabic-speaking users, which allows players to join public or private rooms, meet new people, chat, and play party games together in real time.
Founder Mahmoud Hamed launched the first version of Buzzy Party in April 2025 as a solo developer, but the product has evolved significantly through constant updates and user feedback.
The app combines social interaction with casual games such as trivia, guessing games, drawing games, and social deduction games. The goal is to give people a fun place to spend time with friends or meet new people online.
“I felt there was a lack of social gaming platforms built specifically for Arabic-speaking users. Many international apps support Arabic, but the experience is usually designed for a global audience first,” said Hamed.
“Buzzy Party was designed around the way people in the region socialise and play together online. We compete indirectly with party games, social deduction games, and voice or chat communities, but our focus is bringing social interaction and casual multiplayer games together in one platform.”
The company is completely self-funded, yet Buzzy Game has already reached more than 500,000 installs across iOS and Android.
“Growth has mostly come through word of mouth and organic discovery. We recently passed 500,000 installs, and users spend a significant amount of time in the app. Many users come not only to play games but also to socialise with friends and other members of the community,” Hamed said.
Most of Buzzy Party’s users are currently in Egypt and across the MENA region.
“Going forward, I plan to continue expanding the range of games available on the platform and improve the social features as the community grows. Longer-term, there is also an opportunity to reach Arabic-speaking communities outside the region,” Hamed said.
Revenue currently comes from advertising and in-app purchases.
“Purchases are mainly for cosmetic items, premium features, and additional content. The business generates enough revenue to support operations and infrastructure, and at this stage my main focus remains product growth and user retention,” said Hamed.

articles.title: Kepler Aerospace bags $8M to deploy swarming satellites
articles.text:
Kepler Aerospace bags $8M to deploy swarming satellites
Bengaluru-based Kepler Aerospace will use the seed funding to deploy six swarming ISR satellites and expand its mission operations and avionics businesses.
Kepler Aerospace, a space infrastructure and mission operations company, has raised $8 million in a seed round led by Blue Ashva Capital and co-led by Finvolve India Accelerator and other investors.
The Bengaluru-based firm plans to use the capital primarily to deploy the first six satellites in its autonomous swarming intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance programme under India’s Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) initiative. It has secured two iDEX prime contracts and received about $4 million in grants under the programme.
The fresh funding will also support the expansion of its Mission Operations as a Service and Avionics as a Service businesses, as well as engineering capacity. Over the next 12 to 24 months, the company plans to move into a new facility and add 40 employees.
Kepler’s proposition goes beyond building satellites. It is developing an integrated stack covering satellite systems, avionics, ground infrastructure, mission operations and intelligence delivery.
According to the company, its mission operations platform already serves nearly all Indian space companies, and it operates several ISRO satellites. Its network of more than 70 ground stations provides communications, tracking, telemetry and command functions.
A swarming constellation allows multiple satellites to coordinate their activities, potentially reducing reliance on instructions from a ground station and shortening the time between collecting information and acting on it.
Founder and chief executive officer Navneet Singh said national security will increasingly depend on the ability to “see, understand and respond faster”, adding that achieving this requires satellites, avionics, ground systems and mission operations to function as one system.
Blue Ashva founder Satya Bansal noted that the company’s autonomous architecture could allow satellites to “task each other and act in orbit” without waiting for a ground station.
The fundraise comes as India’s private space industry broadens well beyond launch vehicles. Government data put cumulative private investment in the sector at $618.5 million by March 2026, while the number of registered spacetech startups had reached about 440 by August. Recent funding rounds includes Rs 100 crore by InspeCity, $60 million by unicorn Skyroot, and $20 million by Bellatrix.
Policy has also helped reshape the market, with India opening the sector to private participation in 2020, creating IN-SPACe as the authorising and supervisory body, and subsequently liberalising foreign investment rules for space activities.
The government has also established a Rs 1,000 crore space venture capital fund, alongside seed funding and technology-support programmes. The result is a shift towards a more active ecosystem that is heading towards commercialisation.

articles.title: « Des fonds en attente » : cette nouvelle arnaque vise les Français, la Caisse des Dépôts lance l’alerte
articles.text:
La Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) tire la sonnette d’alarme. Dans un avertissement publié sur son site web, l’institution financière publique indique qu’une vague d’arnaques « au nom de la Caisse des Dépôts » est en cours en France. Le communiqué, publié le lundi 31 août 2026, parle d’une série de tentatives de fraude jouant sur « des fonds en attente », qui n’ont qu’un seul objectif : vous faire payer des faux frais.
À lire aussi : Fuites de données – Lecornu donne « quinze jours » à ses ministres pour riposter
De faux conseillers s’en prennent aux Français
Pour tenter de piéger les Français, les cybercriminels se font passer pour de « faux conseillers Caisse des Dépôts ». Comme toujours, les truands usurpent l’identité d’une entité de confiance pour arriver à leurs fins. L’escroquerie vise des particuliers, qui ne font pas partie des clients de la Caisse des Dépôts.
La cyberattaque s’appuie sur plusieurs méthodes de communication. La cible peut être contactée par téléphone ou par mail. Pour entrer en contact avec ses cibles, les pirates n’ont qu’à piocher dans les innombrables fuites de données de ces dernières années. En agrégeant des répertoires compromis issus du dark web, les pirates peuvent à la fois débusquer des moyens de contacter les Français, mais aussi des informations complémentaires pour rendre l’escroquerie plus crédible.
À lire aussi : Une cyberattaque « sophistiquée » frappe un pôle ministériel, des « mesures particulières » ont été prises
« Des fonds en attente »
Pour attirer l’attention de leurs victimes, les escrocs prétextent « des fonds en attente à la Caisse des Dépôts à la suite d’investissements ». Les pirates affirment que de l’argent est disponible au nom de la victime. Pour rendre leur discours crédible, les fraudeurs s’appuient sur une loi de 2014.
Elle oblige les banques et assureurs à transférer à la Caisse des Dépôts les fonds des comptes inactifs, c’est-à-dire les comptes-titres, PEA, assurances-vie ou plans d’épargne dont le titulaire ne s’est plus manifesté depuis plusieurs années. Concrètement, un compte-titres ou un PEA est transféré à la CDC 10 ans après la dernière opération du client. L’institution conserve ensuite ces sommes d’argent pendant 20 ans dans l’attente qu’un bénéficiaire les réclame. Sur le papier, la démarche paraît logique.
C’est là que le piège se referme. Les pirates demandent à la cible « de verser des frais de dossier pour percevoir les fonds en question ». Sans un versement, la victime ne serait pas en mesure de récupérer l’argent consigné à son intention par la Caisse des Dépôts. Cette exigence permet de déceler qu’il s’agit une arnaque. Si des fonds vous sont réellement dus, aucune institution légitime n’exige de payer pour les récupérer. En fait, elle va simplement prélever les frais sur les fonds qui seront reversés à la personne concernée. Le vrai service de la CDC pour récupérer de l’argent, intitulé Ciclade, est entièrement gratuit et accessible en ligne sans aucun frais préalable.
Dans son avertissement, la Caisse des Dépôts précise bien qu’il faut ignorer les mails, les messages ou les appels de ce genre. Si vous « recevez un appel ou un mail de ce type, n’y donnez pas suite », indique l’organisme. L’institution ajoute que « la Caisse des Dépôts ne contacte jamais ses clients de cette manière ».

articles.title: En su batalla por plantar cara a Renfe, Iryo ha llegado a una conclusión: prefiere Andalucía antes que Barcelona
articles.text:
La verdadera batalla por la alta velocidad se juega en Andalucía. Eso es lo que nos dicen los últimos movimientos de Iryo y Ouigo que han concentrado en esta Comunidad Autónoma gran parte de sus aspiraciones para plantar cara a Renfe. La última en mover ficha ha sido Iryo con un aumento de la oferta que irá directo al sur de España.
Más trenes. Iryo ampliará su oferta en España el año que viene. Lo ha anunciado con un comunicado del que se hacen eco en Europa Press donde se especifica que la compañía italiana contará con más trenes y más frecuencias en las rutas donde ya está establecida.
La empresa ha publicado el volumen de viajes que espera poder realizar a lo largo del año que viene, respaldados por la llegada de tres nuevos trenes que aumenta todavía más la cantidad de viajeros que podrán trasladar a final de año. El objetivo es finalizar el año con 22.764 circulaciones lo que supone un aumento en la oferta del 13,8% respecto a lo dispuesto este año.
Más viajes en el Madrid-Barcelona. Ahora mismo, el corredor Madrid-Barcelona es la línea en la que más asientos ofrece Iryo. La compañía hace tiempo que busca competir con Renfe con inferiores a las del AVE pero claramente superiores a las de Ouigo, según datos de la CNMC. Con más de 7.000 frecuencias, Iryo mantendrá la conexión Madrid-Barcelona como su corredor con mayor trasiego de viajeros.
Sin embargo, los datos de 2025 apuntan a que su capacidad de ocupación de los asientos ofertados fue muy inferior a los de sus rivales. El año pasado se situó en un 77,4% de ocupación de las plazas ofertadas, mientras que Renfe se situó en un 95% y Ouigo en un 94,6%.
Apuntando a Andalucía. Con 3,64 millones de pasajeros el año pasado en el corredor Madrid-Barcelona, es lógico que Iryo siga apostando por la conexión entre las dos mayores ciudades de España. Sin embargo, es en Andalucía donde la compañía aspira a llevar su batalla contra Renfe.
El aumento de la oferta es tal que las plazas en el Madrid-Sevilla crecerán un 39% el año que viene. Y la cifra palidece ante el aumento del 63,7% en el Madrid-Málaga. Estos números llevan a la compañía a parar en un 40% más de ocasiones en Córdoba, parada habitual antes de llegar a ambos destinos.
El año pasado, la ocupación de Iryo en el Madrid-Sevilla y Madrid-Málaga se mantuvo en torno al 75% que experimentan entre Madrid y Barcelona. Sin embargo, la competencia aquí sí cae por debajo del 90%. Y aunque sigue siendo superior a Iryo, están un poco más cerca.
También Ouigo. Además de esta apuesta de Iryo por el sur español, en los últimos meses hemos visto cómo la competencia de Renfe ha ido virando sus posiciones a estos corredores. Y es que Ouigo también prefirió crecer en Andalucía y en este caso, incluso, redujeron sus operaciones en el Madrid-Barcelona.
El verano pasado la compañía francesa confirmó que movía alguno de sus trenes para aumentar la oferta entre Madrid y Sevilla. Y es que su estrategia de precios bajos encaja mejor con este corredor que con el Madrid-Barcelona donde los viajes de negocios suman un enorme grueso de los trayectos que a diario se da entre ambas ciudades.
Un fuerte. Lo que tiene Renfe en el Madrid-Barcelona es un auténtico fuerte. La salida de AVLO por los problemas con sus Talgo podía anticipar ciertos problemas para la compañía ya que se quedaba sin poder pelear en la zona baja de precios. Sin embargo, esto no parece haber hecho tambalear su posición de liderazgo lo más mínimo.
Y es que el corredor entre estas dos ciudades es, con diferencia, el que menos aversión le tiene a los precios altos. El ticket medio el año pasado se situó en 85,07 euros, muy por encima de los 47,59 euros y 45,65 euros del Madrid-Sevilla y Madrid-Málaga con los que se cerró el año pasado. Aunque Renfe ofrece los precios más altos de la línea su tasa de ocupación en este corredor sigue siendo la mejor del mercado.

articles.title: Pourquoi The Witcher 3 Remastered est « gratuit »
articles.text:
C’était l’une des surprises de la cérémonie d’ouverture de la gamescom 2026 : en plus de nouvelles images pour l’extension Songs of the Past, CD Projekt Red a officialisé The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered. Il s’agit d’une nouvelle version améliorée du RPG culte paru en 2015, et la firme polonaise a fait un choix commercial généreux. Tous les propriétaires actuels du jeu n’auront pas besoin de repayer pour en profiter. Rares sont les remasterisations de ce type gratuites (coucou The Last of Us et GTA 5).
CD Projekt Red n’a en réalité jamais songé à facturer The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered. Le co-CEO Michał Nowakowski a révélé pourquoi à l’occasion d’un entretien accordé à The Game Business et publié le 1er septembre 2026. Sur la question de la commercialisation, il a répondu : « Je ne crois pas que c’est une pensée que nous avons eue. Nous le voyons comme une amélioration. » Il explique pourtant que le projet n’a cessé de prendre de l’ampleur à mesure que de plus en plus de choses ont été modifiées, jusqu’à devenir une vraie remasterisation (éclairage, gameplay amélioré, refonte de l’arbre de compétences).
CD Projekt Red nous fait un sacré cadeau avec The Witcher 3 Remastered
Au regard des premières images de ce The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered, on peut croire qu’il s’agit d’un véritable cadeau de la part de CD Projekt Red. Michał Nowakowski appuie ce constat : « Pour nous, c’est vraiment la méthode CDPR, de l’offrir en cadeau aux joueurs qui le possèdent déjà. » Les joueuses et les joueurs qui n’auraient pas encore craqué depuis tout ce temps peuvent, eux, s’offrir l’édition complète du RPG. Pour 50 €, elle réunit le jeu de base et ses deux premières extensions (Hearts of Stone et Blood and Wine).
CD Projekt Red peut aussi se permettre ce geste car The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered va générer de nouveaux revenus avec la sortie, en 2027, de Songs of the Past, un DLC qui sera bel et bien payant. Ce contenu d’envergure, attendu de longue date par les fans, devrait générer des revenus conséquents pour le studio. Il permettra de patienter jusqu’au lancement de The Witcher 4, lequel n’est pas prévu avant 2028.
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered sera disponible à compter du 29 septembre sur PS5, Xbox Series S, Xbox Series X, PC et Nintendo Switch 2. Bonne nouvelle : vos sauvegardes actuelles seront compatibles.

articles.title: Studie zeigt: Chatbots verkaufen dreimal besser als Google-Suche – und du merkst es kaum

Dreifache Klickrate: KI-Bots beeinflussen Käufe stärker als jede Suchmaschine
Dass große Sprachmodelle Menschen gezielt beeinflussen können, sorgt immer wieder für Besorgnis: im politischen Umfeld, wo KI-Content Wahlen beeinflussen könnte, aber auch, weil immer mehr Menschen zunehmend enge persönliche Beziehungen zu ihren Chatbots aufbauen – und so im schlimmsten Fall ihre psychische Gesundheit gefährden. Die Studie ist als Preprint auf der Online-Plattform Arxiv veröffentlicht.

articles.title: Coast Guard Establishes Office of Maritime Cybersecurity Policy
articles.text:
The US Coast Guard has established a dedicated Office of Maritime Cybersecurity Policy as the maritime industry’s growing reliance on information and operational technology expands the cyber risks facing ports, vessels, and other critical infrastructure.
The Office of Maritime Cybersecurity Policy (CG-MCP) will serve as the Coast Guard’s central authority for developing and implementing policies governing the cyber safety and security of the Marine Transportation System (MTS).
Created under the Director of Inspections and Compliance, the office will also serve as the Coast Guard’s primary liaison with industry partners and other government agencies on maritime cybersecurity matters.
Its responsibilities will include developing domestic policy, contributing to international standards, directing a coordinated cybersecurity compliance and enforcement strategy, and engaging with maritime organizations, academia, and national laboratories.
The office will also monitor emerging technologies and techniques that could help the maritime sector proactively manage cyber risk.
“Advanced systems and equipment, including the increased use of information and operational technology, accelerate and transform the maritime industry,” the Coast Guard said. “While these advancements provide operational efficiencies and improvements throughout the Marine Transportation System, they also introduce increased risks to a critical infrastructure sector.”
Rear Adm. Robert C. Compher, assistant commandant for prevention policy, said the Coast Guard must keep pace with the maritime industry’s continued technological advancement.
“The creation of the Office of Maritime Cybersecurity Policy establishes a central authority to develop clear policy, direct a unified compliance strategy, and collaborate with our partners,” Compher said.
The new office is intended to address current threats and vulnerabilities while preparing the maritime sector for emerging cybersecurity challenges, he added.
The announcement comes roughly 18 months after the Government Accountability Office identified multiple shortcomings in the Coast Guard’s approach to securing the MTS, which encompasses roughly 360 commercial sea and river ports.
In a February 2025 report, the watchdog called on the Coast Guard to improve the accuracy of cybersecurity incident information, provide easier access to data on cyber deficiencies, align its cyber plans with the national strategy, establish competency requirements for personnel with MTS cybersecurity responsibilities, and address gaps in those competencies.
The GAO also found that the Coast Guard’s system of record did not provide ready access to complete information about cybersecurity issues uncovered during inspections of vessels and facilities.
Additionally, the agency’s cyber strategy did not fully address several characteristics of an effective national strategy, including risk assessment, performance measures, required resources and investments, and the division of roles and responsibilities.
The Coast Guard did not say whether the creation of the new office was directly related to the GAO findings.

articles.title: NVIDIA and Mediatek Ink $3.5B Investment Deal, Accelerate NVLink Fusion Adoption
articles.text:
Building on a partnership between NVIDIA and MediaTek that has existed for many years, NVIDIA announced this week that it will forge an even deeper partnership with its fellow fabless semiconductor firm. In a major deal that will tie the companies even closer together both financially and technologically, NVIDIA is going to be making a $3.5 billion investment in MediaTek, all the while the Taiwanese semiconductor firm, in turn, will be adopting NVIDIA’s NVLink Fusion platform in order to offer it to MediaTek’s own customers.
Under the terms of the deal, NVIDIA is investing $3.5B in MediaTek by purchasing convertible bonds issued by the company. Meanwhile, on the technology side of matters, MediaTek will be adopting NVIDIA’s complete NVLink Fusion technology stack, the Fusion chiplet, NVLink-C2C, and NVIDIA’s new NVHBM memory protocol, in order to provide it to its own customers. The significance of this technology licensing is that, as MediaTek’s custom silicon business has grown, NVIDIA wants to make its IP readily available to MediaTek’s customers, particularly those working with MediaTek to develop their own XPU accelerator chips.
NVIDIA and MediaTek Ink $3.5B Investment Deal, Accelerate NVLink Fusion Adoption
The deal between NVIDIA and MediaTek comes as MediaTek has become an increasingly significant player in NVIDIA’s orbit. Most notably, MediaTek was NVIDIA’s partner in developing the GB10 SoC, the chip at the heart of NVIDIA’s DGX and RTX Spark boxes. Though officially an NVIDIA chip, MediaTek was responsible for the majority of the chip’s development, most notably its CPU cores and memory controller, while NVIDIA contributed the iGPU and the chip-to-chip connectivity that bonded the two. Consequently, it is not too surprising to see MediaTek and NVIDIA working even more closely together, though the additional investment in MediaTek makes it clear that there is more to this deal than just IP licensing.
In some respects, it is surprising that MediaTek did not ink a larger technology deal with NVIDIA sooner given their close collaboration. MediaTek already uses NVLink-C2C for the GB10, for example. This latest deal is about custom chips rather than MediaTek’s in-house designs, so it is far more involved.
The big takeaway here is that NVIDIA is taking a significant interest in MediaTek’s custom chip business and what it means for XPU development. As hyperscalers and other large AI operators are increasingly developing their own chips, as we have seen with hardware such as Google’s TPUs, Meta’s MTIA, and OpenAI’s Jalapeno, the hyperscalers are increasingly preparing to go their own way in the AI world, or at least, are hedging their bets. So NVIDIA is hedging its bets as well, giving hyperscalers and other custom XPU developers more ready access to the technologies needed to interface with NVIDIA’s ecosystem.
On the technology side of matters then, this means making the complete NVLink Fusion ecosystem available to MediaTek’s customers. NVIDIA has been offering this technology directly to chip designers for some time, but MediaTek’s announcement essentially pushes it one level down the stack by enabling it to offer it directly as well.
The most significant element of this technology offering is the NVLink Fusion chiplet, which NVIDIA has offered since last year. The fabric bridge chip allows chip designers to integrate NVLink support via a UCIe-attached chiplet that provides full-chip NVLink fabric support (while keeping the central components of NVLink as a black box to be integrated rather than licensing the IP itself). This is the critical part to enabling NVLink support on custom XPUs, and allowing those chips to plug into NVLink networks and NVIDIA’s rackscale hardware ecosystem.
The MediaTek deal also includes NVLink-C2C support, NVIDIA’s short-range chip-to-chip connection technology. This is principally used to connect custom CPUs to NVIDIA GPUs (e.g. GB10), but it can also be used to link up multiple XPUs or other chips. Finally, MediaTek will also be offering NVIDIA’s brand-new NVHBM tech, a custom memory protocol intended to connect processors to future generations of HBM, with the memory controller on the base die itself rather than part of the processor.
Aside from NVLink Fusion, the deal between the two companies will also see them continue their current collaborations on Spark devices and automotive projects. In particular, the deal confirms that NVIDIA will not bring the development of future Spark chips in-house, and that MediaTek will continue to play a role over the coming generations, including the Vera Rubin Spark and Rosa Feynman Spark, which are part of NVIDIA’s current roadmap out to 2030.
Final Words
The latest in a series of deals involving NVIDIA and its partners and customers, this week’s MediaTek deal is one of the strongest signs yet that NVIDIA is not content to be just a hardware vendor or even an IP vendor, and that it has greater ambitions to be the backbone of the entire AI industry. Though the MediaTek deal does not bring any new significant technologies to the table that NVIDIA has not already unveiled, it marks another step in their efforts to make NVLink Fusion widely available to other chip vendors.
At the same time, NVIDIA’s increasing use of its profits as a war chest to invest in other companies underscores that they are not just developing technologies and forging partnerships, but also putting their money where their (metaphorical) mouth is. With nearly $60B in profits in their most recent quarter alone, NVIDIA has significant financial resources at its disposal. And now, it would seem, a vision on how they want to use them to bootstrap developments at other tech firms.

articles.title: China sigue perdiendo el liderazgo por la industria de los chips: depende aún de Estados Unidos
articles.text:
La competencia tecnológica entre Estados Unidos y China se concentra en los chips avanzados, componentes esenciales para entrenar modelos de inteligencia artificial, operar centros de datos y sostener la industria digital.
El pulso cobra una dimensión geopolítica por el peso de Taiwán, donde se fabrica la mayor parte de los aceleradores de inteligencia artificial de última generación. Mientras Washington busca limitar el acceso chino a tecnología crítica, Pekín invierte miles de millones de dólares para construir una cadena de semiconductores propia y reducir su dependencia de proveedores occidentales.
PUBLICIDAD
En una entrevista realizada por The Washington Post, el historiador Chris Miller, autor de “La guerra de los chips”, sostuvo que China todavía depende en gran medida de tecnología diseñada y fabricada en Estados Unidos, Europa, Taiwán, Corea del Sur y otros países aliados. Para Miller, la posición inicial favorece a Washington, aunque las restricciones de exportación y el avance industrial chino mantienen abierta la carrera.
La inteligencia artificial elevó el valor estratégico de los chips
La expansión de la inteligencia artificial cambió el mercado de semiconductores. Entrenar y ejecutar modelos avanzados requiere enormes volúmenes de capacidad de cómputo, con chips especializados que procesan datos a gran velocidad. Nvidia domina buena parte de ese segmento, mientras empresas como Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), Samsung e Intel compiten por fabricar componentes cada vez más complejos.
PUBLICIDAD
China lleva más de una década con inversiones públicas y privadas dirigidas a fortalecer su industria local. Empresas como Huawei y Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC) forman parte de esa estrategia. El objetivo es diseñar procesadores, fabricar chips y desarrollar maquinaria propia para disminuir la exposición a controles externos.
A pesar de esos esfuerzos, Miller considera que la producción china de chips de alta gama aún enfrenta dificultades para aumentar su escala. SMIC ha avanzado, pero no alcanza la capacidad tecnológica ni el volumen de TSMC en los procesos más avanzados. La fabricación de semiconductores no depende solo del dinero: exige materiales, herramientas, patentes, técnicos especializados y años de pruebas.
PUBLICIDAD
Los controles de exportación tienen vacíos
Estados Unidos impuso restricciones a la venta de chips y equipos avanzados a compañías chinas. La medida busca impedir que Pekín acceda a hardware útil para aplicaciones militares o para entrenar sistemas de inteligencia artificial de gran escala.
El efecto de esas normas genera debate. Algunas voces de la industria, entre ellas Jensen Huang, director ejecutivo de Nvidia, sostienen que cerrar el mercado chino puede acelerar la creación de alternativas locales. Miller matiza esa visión: el Gobierno chino ya defendía la autosuficiencia tecnológica antes de los controles estadounidenses.
PUBLICIDAD
El problema está en la aplicación de las restricciones. Reportes sobre contrabando de chips y uso de servicios de computación en la nube fuera de China revelan que algunas empresas aún pueden acceder a tecnología estadounidense. Un control que no se aplica de forma efectiva reduce su impacto y crea ventajas para intermediarios y redes informales.
La fabricación de chips depende de máquinas de litografía, capaces de grabar patrones microscópicos sobre obleas de silicio. La empresa neerlandesa ASML domina las herramientas más avanzadas del mercado, en especial las de litografía ultravioleta extrema.
PUBLICIDAD
China trabaja en máquinas propias de litografía DUV, una tecnología anterior pero todavía relevante. El historiador durante la entrevista resaltó que la producción de unas pocas unidades no equivale a dominar una industria que ASML perfeccionó durante décadas.
La dificultad está en llevar esas herramientas a un nivel de rendimiento estable, con bajos márgenes de error y producción masiva. Ese proceso requiere aprendizaje industrial acumulado, proveedores especializados y una cadena internacional que todavía favorece a Occidente y sus aliados.
PUBLICIDAD
Taiwán refuerza su defensa mientras protege su autonomía
Taiwán conserva un papel central en la rivalidad tecnológica. Miller calcula que más del 90% de los aceleradores de IA se fabricará en la isla durante 2026, una concentración que convierte a TSMC en un actor decisivo para empresas estadounidenses y para la economía digital global.
La producción empieza a diversificarse. TSMC ya opera una planta en Arizona y prevé ampliar su presencia en Estados Unidos durante la próxima década. Samsung e Intel también reciben pedidos vinculados al auge de la IA. Aun así, la dependencia de Taiwán seguirá vigente durante años.
PUBLICIDAD
En paralelo, Taipéi propuso destinar 36.000 millones de dólares taiwaneses, cerca de 1.130 millones de dólares, al programa Strong Bow, una versión mejorada de su defensa aérea capaz de interceptar misiles balísticos tácticos. La iniciativa forma parte de un presupuesto de defensa para 2027 que supera los 35.000 millones de dólares y busca fortalecer la soberanía de la isla frente a la presión militar de China.
La carrera por los chips muestra que la competencia entre Estados Unidos y China no se resolverá con un solo avance industrial ni con una restricción comercial aislada. La capacidad para producir semiconductores avanzados depende de cadenas de suministro extensas, conocimiento técnico y una infraestructura que tarda años en consolidarse.

articles.title: Un écran 3D sans lunettes sur un PC portable grand public ? Acer retente le coup avec ce nouveau Aspire
articles.text:
L’écran 3D sans lunette revient visiblement dans l’esprit des constructeurs. Samsung met en avant chaque année son Odyssey 3D alors qu’Acer semble miser beaucoup sur la technologie avec sa gamme SpatialLabs. On se souvient de l’écran Predator View 24 présenté au CES en 2024 qui nous avait à l’époque plutôt bluffé.
Acer réitère en 2026, cette fois sur PC, avec l’Aspire G 3D 16, successeur du Acer Aspire 3D 15 de 2024, présenté à l’IFA 2026, à Berlin. La machine mise tout sur son écran capable d’afficher du relief sans lunettes. Deux caméras suivent les yeux de l’utilisateur pour ajuster l’image en temps réel, pendant qu’un logiciel convertit à la volée n’importe quel contenu 2D en 3D. Photos, vidéos, jeux compatibles : tout peut gagner de la profondeur, sans carte graphique dédiée ni fichier conçu pour la 3D.
L’écran IPS de 16 pouces affiche une définition de 3 840 x 2 400 pixels en 2D, avec un rafraîchissement de 120 Hz et une couverture de 100 % de l’espace colorimétrique DCI-P3. Une dalle taillée pour la retouche photo et la vidéo. Le passage en 3D a toutefois un coût : la définition tombe alors à 1 920 x 2 400 pixels, chaque œil ne recevant que la moitié des pixels. L’application SpatialLabs 3D Hub, préinstallée, gère la conversion et l’accès aux contenus en relief. Dans les jeux compatibles, l’effet sépare plus nettement le premier plan de l’arrière-plan.
Une configuration haut de gamme derrière la 3D
Acer a retenu le processeur AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, couplé à une puce graphique graphique Radeon 8060S intégrée, et la machine peut grimper jusqu’à 128 Go de mémoire LPDDR5x-8000 et 2 To de SSD, des spécificités plutôt rares sur un portable de ce format. La batterie de 99,9 Wh frise d’ailleurs la limite de 100 Wh autorisée en cabine d’avion.
La connectique comprend le Wi-Fi 7, le Bluetooth 5.4 et deux ports USB 4.0 Type-C. Le clavier rétroéclairé RGB reprend les touches WASD rouges appréciées des joueurs, et le lecteur d’empreintes logé dans le bouton d’alimentation reste en option. Le tout prend place dans un châssis métallique gris météorite.
Acer n’a pas encore communiqué de prix ni de date de sortie pour l’Aspire G 3D 16 ; ces informations viendront plus tard. Le modèle rejoint le catalogue de PC portables signés Acer, cette fois avec un écran en relief placé dans une gamme grand public. Il vise d’abord les créateurs et les joueurs curieux de 3D, à condition d’accepter deux limites : la qualité de la conversion dépend du contenu d’origine, et le mode relief réduit la définition de moitié.

articles.title: MTN sees South Africa’s cash economy as MoMo’s next frontier
articles.text:
Cash still dominates everyday payments in South Africa, making it a challenging market for MoMo, MTN’s mobile-money and digital financial services platform. But as the country overhauls its payments infrastructure and opens the market to more competition, the company sees a chance to change how South Africans pay.
MTN wants MoMo to become a broader financial and transactional platform, linking consumers and merchants to payments, credit, remittances and other digital services across its African footprint.
South Africa will serve as an important test of whether the mobile-money model that worked in less banked markets can be adapted to a more mature financial system. MTN believes the answer lies not in competing with banks on basic transactions, but in using the country’s evolving payments infrastructure to build a broader digital financial platform for consumers and merchants.
The strategy includes leveraging new payment infrastructure, pursuing new licences as they become available, and expanding into lending and other financial services. MTN also sees an opportunity among consumers and businesses that continue to rely heavily on cash, as well as smaller merchants that have historically had limited access to financial services.
“The national payments infrastructure is moving very fast. This is infrastructure that we want to leverage to penetrate the market,” MTN Group Fintech chief executive officer (CEO) Serigne Dioum said at the company’s Fintech Summit in Johannesburg on Tuesday.
But South Africa is only one part of the strategy. MTN says MoMo now has more than 70 million monthly active users across 14 markets and processed more than 13 billion transactions worth over $330 billion in the first half of 2026. Its ecosystem includes more than 2.3 million merchants and one million agents, while international remittances exceeded $3 billion during the period.
“We started by giving customers access to financial services. Now we want to move from access to active participation,” Dioum said.
That means customers using their wallets to pay merchants, access loans, save, send money across borders and buy other services. Dioum pointed to Rwanda and Uganda, where customers can send money across borders through MoMo with an experience designed to resemble a domestic transfer.
MTN is also building an open Application Programming Interface (API) that allows partners to integrate their services into its ecosystem. The company says it works with banks, utilities, merchants and other businesses across its markets.
“Africa’s digital economy will increasingly depend on our ability to connect markets, enable cross-border payments, support regional trade and allow people and businesses to participate seamlessly across borders,” Mcebisi Jonas, MTN Group chairman, said.
As MoMo expands into lending, remittances, merchant payments and other financial services, MTN will face greater regulatory requirements around how those services are delivered and how customer money and data are protected.
Lesetja Kganyago, governor of the South African Reserve Bank, said the country’s payments system needs to evolve alongside technology.
“Other countries are ahead of us, and we need to catch up,” Kganyago said.
He said innovation and regulation, particularly in payments, need to work together. The Reserve Bank is moving towards an activity-based regulatory model, under which banks and fintechs offering the same payment services, such as e-money issuance and payment acceptance, would face similar regulatory expectations.
The model would give companies such as MTN more scope to compete in payments while maintaining requirements around consumer protection, safeguarding funds and operational resilience.
“The pace of innovation creates tremendous opportunities for Africa, but sustainable progress depends on ensuring that trust keeps pace,” Nikiwe Tanga, MTN Group Fintech’s chief legal officer, added.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Alertes météo : les cartes de Météo France gagnent en précision pour mieux situer les zones à risques
articles.text:
Alertes météo : les cartes de Météo France gagnent en précision pour mieux situer les zones à risques
Avec la vigilance infradépartementale, Météo France propose dès aujourd'hui d'être plus précis dans son suivi des alertes de types orages, pluies, inondations, neiges, verglas et vents.
Malgré des moyens régulièrement revus à la baisse et des épisodes de vigilance toujours plus nombreux du fait du dérèglement climatique, les équipes de Météo France ne jettent pas l'éponge pour alerter et protéger le grand public. En témoigne la nouveauté déployée ce mardi 1ᵉ septembre. Baptisé vigilance infradépartementale, il s'agit d'un nouveau modèle de carte de vigilance qui devrait aider à mieux s'informer et éviter les catastrophes.
Des prévisions de vigilance plus localisées
Jusqu'à présent, la carte de vigilance de Météo France suivait les lignes des départements pour en colorer l'intégralité en vert, jaune, orange ou rouge selon la situation (orage, pluie, inondation, vent, verglas, neige). Un choix qui s'explique aisément (limitations techniques, de moyens...), mais qui impose cependant un clair manque de précision.
	
La météo n’a que faire des limites administratives, cela fait dix ou quinze ans que la communauté attendait cette évolution.
Désormais, un même département pourra comporter plusieurs couleurs, de manière graduée, "lorsque la situation météorologique prévue le permet avec suffisamment de certitudes". Il s'agira donc véritablement de définir des zones à risques, et non des départements entiers.
Cette nuance permettra ainsi de mieux savoir si la zone où l'on se trouve exactement sera ou non concernée par une alerte. Pour le moment, l'alerte canicule, qui demande un travail supplémentaire, n'est pas concernée par ce nouveau système. Cela pourrait cependant être le cas l'an prochain.
Ce nouveau niveau de précision sera spécialement utile dans les régions montagneuses ou en bord de mer, généralement concernées différemment que les autres. Sur le site de Météo France, l'ancien système restera actif par défaut. Dès qu'une crise sera détectée, l'entièreté du département concerné sera colorée. En revanche, cliquer dessus puis sur le type d'alerte affichera désormais le détail tout juste évoqué.
Sébastien Brana, administrateur du site Infoclimat, précise cependant : "Cela demandera davantage de travail aux prévisionnistes mais ils ont les outils pour le faire, avec des modèles météo aux mailles très fines qui permettent d’affiner les calculs. Il restera cependant une part d’incertitude et il sera toujours impossible de dire, précisément, à quel endroit une tornade va, par exemple, survenir."

articles.title: Aranya raises $11M to turn bare-metal servers into AI clusters in less than 48 hours - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Aranya raises $11M to turn bare-metal servers into AI clusters in less than 48 hours
Aranya Inc., a startup that says it can transform raw bare-metal servers into custom, production-ready graphics processing unit clusters for artificial intelligence inference in less than two days, launched today with $11 million in funding.
The company says it’s addressing a critical bottleneck in the AI infrastructure market. Founded last year, Aranya says it has already been tasked with managing more than $500 million worth of GPU hardware for leading AI inference providers and data centers.
Its flagship technology is an open-source engine called clusterdOS, built on top of Kubernetes, that provides a framework for deploying and maintaining infrastructure through declarative configuration files. It also automates the orchestration of containerized workloads, networking and storage resources across various hardware environments.
“ClusterdOS is built for organization-scale computing, not for managing individual applications or isolated workloads,” Christian Bhatia Ondaatje, co-founder and CEO of Aranya, said in a written response to questions about the platform’s capabilities.
Aranya said it addresses Kubernetes’ shortcomings in two critical areas. While Kubernetes can reschedule a pod off a failing node, it does not diagnose the root cause. “ClusterdOS discovers, diagnoses and resolves the hardware itself,” Ondaatje said.
That includes GPU thermal events, error-correcting code errors and networking faults. The engine is also not Kubernetes-exclusive. It also encompasses virtual machine-based and the Simple Linux Utility for Resource Management job schedules and workload manager. “Real GPU infrastructure is heterogeneous and the OS layer has to absorb that,” Ondaatje said.
The company promises it can transform any quantity of racked hardware into a cohesive, self-healing cluster within 48 hours, including custom storage and networking. “We’ve matched that timeline repeatedly, and no other operator does it consistently for custom architecture,” Ondaatje said.
ClusterdOS provides federated control across multiple clusters. The system is designed to autonomously detect and remediate issues before they escalate, using agents that “live inside the cluster continuously and adapt to what that cluster needs,” rather than executing pre-scripted jobs, Ondaatje said.
Strict controls
To prevent accidental disruption, the OS operates under strict permission controls. “The multicluster OS cannot see or access anything the organization hasn’t explicitly granted it,” he said. “It’s governed by strict multitenancy and role-based permissions at the OS level. Access is granted, not assumed.”
Aranya is also introducing a natural-language interface that allows engineers to manage infrastructure using plain commands, such as spinning up inference endpoints or adding nodes, without touching configuration files. The system respects existing user permissions to ensure that actions are both secure and auditable. “A request in Slack resolves to the same permitted action set the engineer already has,” said Ondaatje.
The company is also claiming significant operational improvements from the use of its software. The most notable are what Ondaatje called “dramatic reductions in downtime at both the cluster and datacenter scale, achieved through proactive symptom detection.
The federated architecture also allows teams to manage all their clusters as a unified fleet, while built-in utilization monitoring helps rightsize workloads and optimize costs. Aranya’s system also enables customers to recycle idle compute, further reducing operating expenses.
With the fresh capital, Aranya plans to expand its engineering and sales/marketing teams and launch a full multicluster interface. The round includes a $9 million seed led by First Round Capital Holdings L.P. with participation from BoxGroup Ventures LLC, Vermilion Cliffs Ventures LLC and Asylum Ventures and a $2 million pre-seed round led by Asylum Ventures.
